answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, slashable deposit in a public vault before it can earn fees or vote. Existing agents select random peers for cross-checks, and a fraud proof burns the suspect’s deposit while rewarding the reporter. Reputation also grows slowly with successful trades, so splitting into many fresh identities resets earning history. An attacker therefore pays capital for every Sybil, risks losing it to audits, and cannot cheaply multiply influence across the cedar trellis of trust.
